items.question: What does reading a stored value that matches no status or known old spelling return?
items.ticket: Existing values are normalised when read
items.chose: Returns null instead of throwing or guessing the nearest status.
items.instead: Throw an error, or fall back to a default such as draft.

items.question: Does writing a status normalise near-miss input (wrong case, padding, old spellings), or reject it?
items.chose: Accepts only an exact enum value and throws an Error for anything else, including 'Draft', ' draft' and 'in-review'.
items.instead: Normalise the input with the read logic and write the canonical value, or return null instead of throwing.

items.question: How much cleanup is applied to a stored value before matching it (case, whitespace, separators)?
items.ticket: Existing values are normalised when read
items.chose: Trims the ends, lowercases, and collapses runs of space, '-' and '_' into one space, then trims again. Edge separators are stripped, so '-draft-' reads as draft.
items.instead: Only trim and lowercase, or treat '-' and '_' as part of the value.

items.question: Which old spellings map to which statuses?
items.ticket: Sandbox status is stored as free text (draft, Draft, in-review...)
items.chose: Maps only the cleaned form 'in review' to review. Any other legacy value (e.g. 'in progress', 'done') reads as null.
items.instead: Include more aliases such as 'pending' or 'open', or have no alias table and match only the case-insensitive enum.

items.question: Can internal separators join a status's letters, so that 'mer_ged' or 'dr aft' reads as a status?
items.chose: No. Separators become a single space, so 'mer___ged' and 'dr aft' become 'mer ged' and 'dr aft' and read as null.
items.instead: Strip separators entirely before matching, so 'mer_ged' reads as merged.

items.question: Does a bulk read of many rows stop at an unreadable row or keep going?
items.chose: Keeps going. Every row is returned, an unreadable row gets status null, and its id is kept.
items.instead: Throw on the first unreadable row, or drop unreadable rows from the result.

items.question: How are unreadable values reported by the bulk read: raw or cleaned, and are duplicates removed?
items.chose: Reports the raw stored strings, so 'zebra' and 'zebra ' stay separate. They are de-duplicated with a Set and sorted.
items.instead: Report cleaned values, or the ids of the bad rows, or keep duplicates in row order.

items.question: In what order are the unreadable values listed?
items.chose: Default string sort, which is by UTF-16 code unit. Uppercase sorts before lowercase.
items.instead: Keep first-seen order, or sort case-insensitively or by locale.

items.question: What does reading an empty or whitespace-only value return?
items.chose: Returns null, because it cleans to an empty string that matches nothing.

items.question: What does the bulk read return for an empty list of rows?
items.chose: Returns an empty rows array and an empty unreadable array.
items.instead: Throw, or return null or undefined.

items.question: What does the error message for a rejected write contain?
items.chose: Throws a plain Error with the message 'not a sandbox status: ' followed by the JSON-quoted value.
items.instead: Throw a custom error class (e.g. a TypeError or RangeError), or list the allowed values in the message.
